<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches source code from declared GitHub repositories associated with the project (ZL-Audio), including the main plugin, a JUCE framework commit, and an FFT library. All sources are pinned to specific commits or tags, and SHA-256 checksums are provided and match standard practice. The prepare() function reorganizes downloaded submodules (JUCE and zldsp_fft) into the correct directory structure, which is a common requirement for CMake-based builds using FetchContent or similar mechanisms. It also patches the CMakeLists.txt to use the system's highway library, avoiding bundled dependencies—a sound security and packaging practice.

The build process uses standard CMake invocation with ninja, compiles the code with clang, and disables forced rpath installation. It explicitly sets `FETCHCONTENT_FULLY_DISCONNECTED=ON`, ensuring no network access during the build, which mitigates supply-chain risks from unexpected downloads. The resulting packages install only the built VST3 and LV2 plugin binaries into standard system directories, following Audio Plugin conventions. No suspicious commands (e.g., `curl|bash`, `eval`, obfuscated code) are present. All operations stay within the build directory and target `$pkgdir`.

No evidence of data exfiltration, dynamic code loading, or execution of third-party scripts is found. The source URLs, while not pinned to git commits in the URL, use tagged releases (`${pkgver}`) and are verified via checksums. The use of fixed git commits for dependencies further improves reproducibility. This PKGBUILD follows secure and standard AUR packaging practices.
</details>
